questions.question: Intermolecular forces are:
options: The covalent bonds inside each molecule
The forces holding protons in the nucleus
The attractions between separate molecules, far weaker than covalent bonds

questions.question: When water boils, what is overcome?
options: The intermolecular forces between water molecules — the molecules themselves stay intact
The covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen
Both the covalent bonds and the intermolecular forces
The forces inside the oxygen nucleus

questions.question: Breaking INTRAmolecular bonds is:
options: A chemical change that destroys the substance

questions.question: A substance whose molecules grip each other strongly will tend to have:
options: A low boiling point and rapid evaporation
High melting and boiling points and slow evaporation

questions.question: London (induced dipole) forces exist because:
options: Moving electrons form fleeting temporary dipoles that induce matching dipoles in neighbours

questions.question: Fluorine and chlorine are gases, bromine a liquid and iodine a solid because:
options: London forces strengthen as the molecules grow larger with more electrons
The lighter halogens repel each other

questions.question: Hydrogen bonding is possible only when hydrogen is covalently bonded to:
Ranked from weakest to strongest, the intermolecular forces run:

subtopics.title: Boiling Points, Vapour Pressure and the Water Anomaly

questions.question: Light water boils at 100 °C while heavier hydrogen sulfide boils at −60 °C because:
options: Water hydrogen-bonds and hydrogen sulfide cannot — force type beats molecular size

questions.question: A liquid with WEAK intermolecular forces shows:
options: High vapour pressure, fast evaporation and a low boiling point
Low vapour pressure and a high boiling point
No evaporation below its boiling point

questions.question: Ice floats on liquid water because:
options: Freezing breaks half the covalent bonds
Hydrogen bonds lock the solid into an open lattice less dense than the liquid
Ice is warmer than the water below it
All solids float on their own liquids

questions.question: Propanone feels cold on the skin because:
options: It is stored in cold cupboards
It reacts with the skin's surface
Its weakly-held molecules evaporate rapidly, drawing heat from the skin

subtopics.title: Dissolving, Ion-Dipole Forces and Like Dissolves Like

questions.question: When sodium chloride dissolves in water, the ions are prised from the lattice by:
options: Ion-dipole attractions between the ions and the charged ends of water molecules

questions.question: Around a dissolved sodium ion, water molecules orient themselves with:
options: Their hydrogen sides toward the positive ion
Their negative oxygen corners toward the positive ion
Their oxygen corners pointing away from the ion

questions.question: Candle wax dissolves in petrol because:
options: Both are non-polar and trade comparable London forces

questions.question: Wax will NOT dissolve in water because:
options: Wax molecules are too large to move
Water molecules grip one another with hydrogen bonds far stronger than anything wax can offer

subtopics.title: The Glue Between, Not the Glue Within

questions.question: In the brick wall picture, the bricks and the mortar stand for:
options: Chemical bonds inside molecules and the weaker forces between molecules

questions.question: The steam above boiling water consists of:
options: Intact water molecules that have escaped their neighbours

questions.question: Surgical spirits dries off the skin in seconds while water lingers because:
options: Spirits is always colder than water
Its molecules barely grip each other, while water clings to itself strongly

questions.question: The "flicker" grade of stickiness corresponds to:
options: London forces from momentary shifts of the electron cloud

questions.question: Large non-polar molecules like candle wax can be solids because:
options: Many weak flickers across a big molecule add up to a real grip

questions.question: The hydrogen bond is best described as:
options: A true covalent bond between molecules
A strong intermolecular force, about a tenth the strength of a covalent bond
A force present in every molecule

questions.question: Without hydrogen bonding, water at room temperature would be:

subtopics.title: Why Salt Disappears and Oil Refuses

questions.question: A dissolved ion travels through the water surrounded by:
options: Other ions of the same charge
A shell of oriented water molecules — its hydration escort

questions.question: Oil floats on water instead of dissolving because:
options: Water would have to break its own hydrogen bonds and gain no comparable attraction in return

questions.question: Grease that water cannot shift comes out in dry-cleaning fluid because:
options: Both grease and the fluid are non-polar — like dissolves like
The fluid boils the grease away
Grease reacts chemically with the fluid

questions.question: A complete explanation of any solubility observation must name:
options: The forces in the solute, in the solvent, and between them, and whether the exchange pays
The melting points of both substances
